correctness.rationale: Direct two-arc integration gives a real Toeplitz four-by-four Gram. Reversal symmetry yields two explicit two-by-two blocks. Their shifted determinant average is identically -4 A^2 sin(alpha)^2 cos(theta/2)^4/3, so a block has a negative shifted eigenvalue; the max row-sum 4A gives the global gap. At antipodal placement the Gram spectrum has two copies of m-B and two of m+B. The smallest eigenvalues of the two blocks have opposite slopes +-2A sin(alpha)^2 in x=cos(theta/2), giving the sharp delta-angle coefficient A sin(alpha)^2=2 sin(alpha)^3/pi. Verified algebraically and by an independently assembled quadrature Gram in 246 cases; universal proof is analytic. Domains include endpoint theta=2alpha and exclude alpha=0,pi/2.

value.rationale: The problem measures worst-case recovery from two finite-aperture circular observation windows. Unlike an exact optimizer alone, the global deficit provides a positive, nonasymptotic tolerance estimate for any center misplacement, and the sharp first-order cusp determines the exact local sensitivity. The doubled weakest-eigenvalue multiplicity gives a structural explanation for the nondifferentiability. The result is not asserted for arbitrary bands and is not a routine reparameterization of the three-character scalar optimum.
